newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian police arrest former Bankcoop bank head.
newsitem.headline: Romanian police arrest former Bankcoop bank head.

text.p: Romanian police have arrested Alexandru Dinulescu, former boss of private Bankcoop bank, on charges of bribe-taking, police officials said on Thursday.

"Dinulescu, like other bankers, was arrested on grounds of bribe taking," police spokesman Haralambie Neda told Reuters. Dinulescu was accused of taking some $75,000 in order to grant illegal credits to unnamed companies in 1993 and 1994.

He was the second bank president arrested since the 1989 fall of communism. Marcel Ivan, former boss of troubled Credit Bank SA private bank, was arrested in 1995 for deriving unearned gains and spent one year in detention.

An arrest warrant for 30 days was issued against Dinulescu pending completion of investigations over bribe-taking, a charge which incurs up to 15 years in jail, Neda said. Official charges have yet to be pressed.

On the eve of his arrest Dinulescu resigned as president of Banca de Credit Cooperatist Bankcoop SA, without giving a reason. Bankcoop officials told Reuters that Dinulescu was still a member of the bank's board.
"A decision to remove Dinulescu from the bank board is yet to be made," Bankcoop spokesman Auras Albu said. He said he did not believe that the arrest would affect the bank.
Earlier this year Dinulescu was locked in a row with Bankcoop's main shareholder, leading businessman George Paunescu, over funding for his majority stake in the bank.
Last week the central bank cleared the transaction, saying that Paunescu's $10 million stock acquisition had been correct.
The row sparked queues at the bank's offices earlier this year when people rushed to withdraw their money, but panic subsided soon.
Bankcoop reported an end-1996 provisional balance sheet of 2.1 trillion lei ($289.9 million), 870 billion lei up from 1995 and a 1996 gross profit of 66 billion ($9.3 million). ($=7,744 lei)
